subject: Renewal: hot-pool + autoscale SLOs (proposal)
messages:
From: Jared Lambert <jared.lambert@acme-corp.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal: hot-pool + autoscale SLOs

Hi Tessa,

As we approach our 12/01 renewal, we've been modeling traffic for Q1 and expect a ~2.5x increase in peak token throughput for a couple of critical flows. To avoid customer impact we want to add committed capacity on Dedicated and request a small "hot pool" that keeps N GPUs continuously warm so scale-up is sub-30s. Couple asks:

- Add 8 GPUs to the reserved pool (preferably the same instance type)
- Hot pool of 2 GPUs to eliminate cold-starts for our 99th pct spikes
- Maintain a throughput guarantee of 120k tokens/sec across committed capacity with credits for any shortfall
- Short scale-up lag (target <= 30s to spin from warm pool to full capacity)

Can Redwood provide a proposed amendment (capacity + SLA language) and ballpark uplift to MSRP? Procurement will need the formal amendment and an updated PO.

Thanks,
Jared
Jared Lambert
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Renewal: hot-pool + autoscale SLOs

- Draft amendment + PO-ready summary for Procurement

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal: hot-pool + autoscale SLOs — feasibility notes

Tessa / team — quick technical readout after a short simulation against ACME's QPS profile:

Summary recommendations (safe starting point):
- Reserved commit: +8 same-class GPUs (pinned to the customer's pool)
- Hot pool: 2 GPUs kept in a warmed state (KV cache preloaded) — purpose: reduce first-token latency for burst windows
- Autoscale policy: min_replicas = 4 (baseline for steady-state), max_replicas = 20 (headroom for 2.5x traffic)
- Warm pool lifecycle: keep hot GPUs in steady state for at least 30 minutes between rapid burst events (configurable)
- Scale-up lag target: 25s median, 45s P95 measured from trigger to first token served on scaled replica (with hot pool present we should hit ~25s)
- Fallback: if scale-up exceeds 60s we failover to pre-warmed model variant on alternative pool (costly but available)

Operational notes:
- We will need an explicit OLA on how prefix-KV caching is primed for the hot pool — recommend a background warm-up job that periodically replays representative prefixes (customer to approve sample prompts).
- Monitoring hooks: token-rate per replica, scale events, warm-pool utilization. We'll expose alerts for scale-lag > 40s.

I can produce a short SLA matrix with measurable KPIs for Marissa to use in the amendment.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T14:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal: hot-pool + autoscale SLOs — commercial proposal

Team — based on Aditya's parameters, here's the commercial approach I suggest:

- Capacity uplift: 8 additional committed GPUs (same SKU) — term: 12 months (aligned to renewal)
- Hot pool: 2 GPUs — billed as a reserved hotpool line item at 45% of a full-GPU rate (reflects the warmed-state benefit and lower cumulative utilization risk)
- Throughput guarantee: 120k tokens/sec across the committed pool; shortfall credit = 5% monthly credit per hour of verified breach, capped at 40% of that month's committed capacity cost
- Scale-up SLA: median <= 30s, P95 <= 50s. If P95 > 50s for a given month we apply the shortfall credit for SLA breach (same cap rules as above)
- Price uplift: ~+18% on committed spend for the hot pool + guaranteed throughput add-on; we can offer an introductory 3-month waiver on the hot-pool line item to ease the transition

Action items:
- I'll draft the term amendment (with SLA matrix) and attach the change form.
- Tessa: recommend we propose a single-signature amendment to speed Procurement.

Marissa
Director, Renewals
Redwood Inference

Tessa — the proposal looks good at a glance. Two quick clarifications before passing to procurement:

1) We prefer the 8 GPUs to be fully committed (not burst).
2) Can you add an explicit clause that the warm-up job will only use anonymized/sample prefixes and that Acme can opt-out of any replay material? We need that in writing for our privacy team.

If you can add those two items, I'll get Procurement to route the PO next week and we can e-sign. Thanks for moving fast on this.

—Jared
